doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Total J.J. and J.J.! RCA albums for producer Jack Somer
summary: Somer told Johnson to write everything and feature himself on the RCA big band albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Maybe this would be the time – even though it goes a little out of order, Lida, with what you’re doing – to look at the other larger works, particularly the works that comprised the two big band albums you did where you did Stratusphunk and those things. [Let's] talk a little bit about your writing for the bigger ensembles, either the larger works in the sense of Poem for Brass or the big band works that comprised those two albums – Little Dave, Swing Spring, Stratusphunk, some of those things. [The albums are The Total J. J. Johnson and J.J.!]
Yeah. Actually there were two different albums. Then it came out again under just J.J.
It had a lot of stuff on it. Fact is, you do Stolen Moments on that.
Right. Oliver Nelson's Stolen Moments. Right. The producer on those occasions I remember was Jack Somer, S-O-M-E-R.

He said, "J.J., on this recording project I would like for you to write all the material and to primarily feature yourself, so it's really J.J. Johnson’s baby." Da-da-da-dah. So I did sit down and write all these arrangements and whatever originals came out of that scenario.
